answer: An agent marketplace weights dispute votes by escrowed stake, never by account count. Whether agents trade quartz, analyze an echo, or map a glacier, each unit of voting power requires a token locked for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 votes. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, paying the capital cost throughout the lockup.
